newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada-Chicago gas pipe faces approval next week.
newsitem.headline: Canada-Chicago gas pipe faces approval next week.

text.p: The partnership of Canadian energy companies hoping to build a C$3.6-billion pipeline to Chicago from northern Canada plans to decide next week whether it has enough gas committed to proceed with the project, its top officer said on Tuesday.

However, Dennis Cornelson, chief executive of Alliance Pipeline, predicted the 1.25 billion cubic feet per day project would get the green light to submit regulatory filings in Canada and the United States after a board meeting on November 26.
Alliance, a group of 18 companies including Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and IPL Energy Inc.

The partnership is currently scouring the commitments to ship gas that were made during its open season that ended on November 8. Time is being taken by examining the credit of shippers and special requests that were made, Cornelson said.
"All I can say is that I'm confident that we will proceed with the construction of the Alliance pipeline," he told reporters following a speech to a natural gas conference.

The company's plans including submitting an application with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission before the end of this year and another with Canada's National Energy Board in mid-1997. The liquids-rich gas pipeline is scheduled to be in service in 1999.
"The regulatory climate in Washington is very, very positive for this and the concept of having competition amongst Canadian pipelines is something that they would feel good about," he said.
The Alliance project is a main participant in the current Canadian battle over expanding gas pipeline capacity out of the country.
Producers have criticized traditional pipeline companies such as NOVA Corp and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd for not expanding capacity to allow higher prices for Canadian gas.
Another producer, PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, has proposed a pipeline in southern Alberta that would bring competition into the province after decades of the industry being dominated by NOVA.

Cornelson said on Tuesday that Alliance, NOVA and PanCanadian, proponent of the southern Alberta Palliser Pipeline, met last Wednesday with the Alberta government's Standing Committee on Energy and Sustainable Development for an often heated discussion on the effects of pipeline competition on the province.
The government, which stands to be caught in the crossfire between the opposing forces, has not announced a position on how competition should be allowed in Alberta.
